fields.Front: Case study: give the attributes of each entity, marking keys and special kinds.
fields.Back:
DEPARTMENT: Name (key), Number (key), Locations (MULTI-VALUED) - two keys, unusual.
EMPLOYEE: SSN (key), Name (possibly composite), Address, Salary, Sex, Birthdate (Age would be derived).
PROJECT: Number (key), Name (key), Location (single-valued - 'a single location').
DEPENDENT: Name, Sex, Birthdate, Relationship - no key of its own (weak entity).

fields.Front: Which words in the case-study specification tell you an attribute is a key or multi-valued?
fields.Back: 'Each department has a unique name, number' -> Name and Number are KEYS. 'A department may have SEVERAL locations' -> Locations is MULTI-VALUED. 'A single location' for a project rules multi-valued out. The verbs (manages, controls, works on, supervisor, dependents of) are relationships, not attributes.

fields.Front: Case study: which relationship carries Hours, which carries StartDate, and why are they not on the entities?
fields.Back: Hours is on WORKS ON: 'how many hours did an employee work on a project?' depends on the (employee, project) pair. StartDate is on MANAGES: it could sit on either entity because MANAGES is 1:1, but it describes the ACT OF MANAGING, so it stays on the diamond.

fields.Front: APPLICATION: a car-rental mini-world says 'every rental is for exactly one car; a customer may have many rentals; each rental records the pick-up date'. Where does the pick-up date go, and what is the cardinality?
fields.Back: Pick-up date describes the rental itself, i.e. the (customer, car) association, so it belongs on the RELATIONSHIP, not on CUSTOMER or CAR. CUSTOMER (1) --- rents --- (M) CAR in this reading: a customer may rent many cars over time, each rental instance for one car.

fields.Front: APPLICATION: 'Keep track of when the employee started managing the department.' Which noun is only implied and where does it end up?
fields.Back: DATE - it is never named as a noun in the list, but 'when' means a date must be stored. It becomes the StartDate attribute on the MANAGES relationship (not on EMPLOYEE or DEPARTMENT).

fields.Front: Summarise the finished case-study ER diagram in words.
fields.Back:
EMPLOYEE 1 --- MANAGES (StartDate) --- 1 DEPARTMENT (employee partial, department total)
EMPLOYEE N --- WORKS FOR --- 1 DEPARTMENT (both total)
DEPARTMENT 1 --- CONTROLS --- N PROJECT (department partial, project total)
EMPLOYEE M --- WORKS ON (Hours) --- N PROJECT (both total)
EMPLOYEE 1 --- SUPERVISES --- N EMPLOYEE, unary (both partial)
EMPLOYEE 1 === HAS === N DEPENDENT, double diamond, DEPENDENT weak and total, partial key Name
DEPARTMENT has the multi-valued attribute Locations

fields.Front: APPLICATION: a hospital mini-world says 'a doctor attends many patients and a patient may be attended by many doctors; each attendance records the date'. Name the entities, the relationship, its degree, ratio and attribute.
fields.Back: Entities DOCTOR and PATIENT; relationship ATTENDS (a verb); degree 2 (binary); ratio M:N; the date is an attribute ON the relationship diamond, because it depends on the (doctor, patient) pair, not on either alone.

fields.Text: The case-study entities are {{c1::DEPARTMENT}}, {{c1::EMPLOYEE}}, {{c1::DEPENDENT}} and PROJECT; everything else in the specification is either an attribute or a relationship.

Case study attributes: DEPARTMENT has keys {{c1::Name and Number}} plus the multi-valued {{c1::Locations}}; EMPLOYEE's key is {{c1::SSN}}; PROJECT has keys Number and Name and a single Location; DEPENDENT has no key of its own.
